items.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: I saw Anita O’Day with Gene Krupa on the stage

ctx.x: Teddy Wilson piano; Earl “Fatha” Hines’ big band; Woody Herman’s Thundering Herd; Sonny Stitt, Charlie Parker, Dizzy Gillespie, Miles Davis.

As we go, you go. I started out without even a record player listening to the radio. I’m talking about Jo Stafford and you know there were a few people, just hearing songs, good songs, and the singers were pretty good and I could learn them from the radio. And then also getting into more jazz things because I started working with bands around Milwaukee. You know playing stock arrangements most of the time, but I did get to meet a lot of musicians, and they’d say, “hey have you ever heard Billie Holiday — have you…

I would listen to late night radio, I was supposed to be asleep but I would take a small radio under my covers, one of those little radios, and I would listen to Earl “Fatha” Hines broadcast from the Grand Terrace Ballroom in Chicago. And they would come on the air and you’d hear like [scats] and the brass is like [scats]. And then over all this you hear this voice come in and he says “Fatha Hines, Earl, Fatha Hines.” [scats] And I’d listen and and oh God, that’s so wonderful, that’s what I want to do. And I was…
